# PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS] Contents of this Part

## Scope of this Part

## 31.1

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.1] (1) This Part sets out rules about the disclosure and inspection of documents. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.1] (2) This Part applies to all claims except a claim on the small claims track. ## Meaning of disclosure

## 31.2 A party discloses a document by stating that the document exists or has existed. ## Right of inspection of a disclosed document

## 31.3

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.3] (1) A party to whom a document has been disclosed has a right to inspect that document except where –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.3] (a) the document is no longer in the control of the party who disclosed it;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.3] (b) the party disclosing the document has a right or a duty to withhold inspection of it, or

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.3] (c) paragraph (2) applies. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.3] (Rule 31.8 sets out when a document is in the control of a party)

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.3] (Rule 31.19 sets out the procedure for claiming a right or duty to withhold inspection)

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.3] (2) Where a party considers that it would be disproportionate to the issues in the case to permit inspection of documents within a category or class of document disclosed under rule 31.6(b) –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.3] (a) he is not required to permit inspection of documents within that category or class; but

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.3] (b) he must state in his disclosure statement that inspection of those documents will not be permitted on the grounds that to do so would be disproportionate. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.3] (Rule 31.6 provides for standard disclosure)

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.3] (Rule 31.10 makes provision for a disclosure statement)

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.3] (Rule 31.12 provides for a party to apply for an order for specific inspection of documents)

## Meaning of document

## 31.4 In this Part –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.4 In this Part –] ‘document’ means anything in which information of any description is recorded; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.4 In this Part –] ‘copy’, in relation to a document, means anything onto which information recorded in the document has been copied, by whatever means and whether directly or indirectly. ## Disclosure

## 31.5

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (1) Omitted

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (2) Unless the court otherwise orders, paragraphs (3) to (8) apply to all intermediate and multi-track claims, other than those which include a claim for personal injuries. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (3) Not less than 14 days before the first case management conference, if any, each party must file and serve a report verified by a statement of truth, which –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (a) describes briefly what documents exist or may exist that are or may be relevant to the matters in issue in the case;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (b) describes where and with whom those documents are or may be located;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (c) in the case of electronic documents, describes how those documents are stored;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (d) estimates the broad range of costs that could be involved in giving standard disclosure in the case, including the costs of searching for and disclosing any electronically stored documents; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (e) states which of the directions under paragraphs (7) or (8) are to be sought. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (4) In cases where the Electronic Documents Questionnaire has been exchanged, the Questionnaire should be filed with the report required by paragraph (3). [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (5) Not less than seven days before the first case management conference, and on any other occasion as the court may direct, the parties must, at a meeting or by telephone, discuss and seek to agree a proposal in relation to disclosure that meets the overriding objective. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (6) If –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (a) the parties agree proposals for the scope of disclosure; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (b) the court considers that the proposals are appropriate in all the circumstances,

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] the court may approve them without a hearing and give directions in the terms proposed. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (7) At the first or any subsequent case management conference, the court will decide, having regard to the overriding objective and the need to limit disclosure to that which is necessary to deal with the case justly, which of the following orders to make in relation to disclosure –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (a) an order dispensing with disclosure;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (b) an order that a party disclose the documents on which it relies, and at the same time request any specific disclosure it requires from any other party;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (c) an order that directs, where practicable, the disclosure to be given by each party on an issue by issue basis;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (d) an order that each party disclose any documents which it is reasonable to suppose may contain information which enables that party to advance its own case or to damage that of any other party, or which leads to an enquiry which has either of those consequences;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (e) an order that a party give standard disclosure;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (f) any other order in relation to disclosure that the court considers appropriate. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (8) The court may at any point give directions as to how disclosure is to be given, and in particular –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (a) what searches are to be undertaken, of where, for what, in respect of which time periods and by whom and the extent of any search for electronically stored documents;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (b) whether lists of documents are required;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (c) how and when the disclosure statement is to be given;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (d) in what format documents are to be disclosed (and whether any identification is required);

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (e) what is required in relation to documents that once existed but no longer exist; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (f) whether disclosure shall take place in stages. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.5] (9) To the extent that the documents to be disclosed are electronic, the provisions of Practice Direction 31B – Disclosure of Electronic Documents will apply in addition to paragraphs (3) to (8). ## Standard disclosure – what documents are to be disclosed

## 31.6 Standard disclosure requires a party to disclose only–

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.6 Standard disclosure requires a party to disclose only–] (a) the documents on which he relies; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.6 Standard disclosure requires a party to disclose only–] (b) the documents which –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.6 Standard disclosure requires a party to disclose only–] (i) adversely affect his own case;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.6 Standard disclosure requires a party to disclose only–] (ii) adversely affect another party’s case; or

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.6 Standard disclosure requires a party to disclose only–] (iii) support another party’s case; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.6 Standard disclosure requires a party to disclose only–] (c) the documents which he is required to disclose by a relevant practice direction. ## Duty of search

## 31.7

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.7] (1) When giving standard disclosure, a party is required to make a reasonable search for documents falling within rule 31.6(b) or (c). [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.7] (2) The factors relevant in deciding the reasonableness of a search include the following –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.7] (a) the number of documents involved;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.7] (b) the nature and complexity of the proceedings;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.7] (c) the ease and expense of retrieval of any particular document; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.7] (d) the significance of any document which is likely to be located during the search. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.7] (3) Where a party has not searched for a category or class of document on the grounds that to do so would be unreasonable, he must state this in his disclosure statement and identify the category or class of document. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.7] (Rule 31.10 makes provision for a disclosure statement)

## Duty of disclosure limited to documents which are or have been in a party’s control

## 31.8

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.8] (1) A party’s duty to disclose documents is limited to documents which are or have been in his control. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.8] (2) For this purpose a party has or has had a document in his control if –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.8] (a) it is or was in his physical possession;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.8] (b) he has or has had a right to possession of it; or

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.8] (c) he has or has had a right to inspect or take copies of it. ## Disclosure of copies

## 31.9

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.9] (1) A party need not disclose more than one copy of a document. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.9] (2) A copy of a document that contains a modification, obliteration or other marking or feature –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.9] (a) on which a party intends to rely; or

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.9] (b) which adversely affects his own case or another party’s case or supports another party’s case;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.9] shall be treated as a separate document. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.9] (Rule 31.4 sets out the meaning of a copy of a document)

## Procedure for standard disclosure

## 31.10

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (1) The procedure for standard disclosure is as follows. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (2) Each party must make and serve on every other party, a list of documents in the relevant practice form. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (3) The list must identify the documents in a convenient order and manner and as concisely as possible. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (4) The list must indicate –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (a) those documents in respect of which the party claims a right or duty to withhold inspection; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (b)

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (i) those documents which are no longer in the party’s control; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (ii) what has happened to those documents. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (Rule 31.19 (3) and (4) require a statement in the list of documents relating to any documents inspection of which a person claims he has a right or duty to withhold)

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (5) The list must include a disclosure statement. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (6) A disclosure statement is a statement made by the party disclosing the documents –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (a) setting out the extent of the search that has been made to locate documents which he is required to disclose;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (b) certifying that he understands the duty to disclose documents; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (c) certifying that to the best of his knowledge he has carried out that duty. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (7) Where the party making the disclosure statement is a company, firm, association or other organisation, the statement must also–

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (a) identify the person making the statement; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (b) explain why he is considered an appropriate person to make the statement. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (8) The parties may agree in writing –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (a) to disclose documents without making a list; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (b) to disclose documents without the disclosing party making a disclosure statement. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.10] (9) A disclosure statement may be made by a person who is not a party where this is permitted by a relevant practice direction. ## Duty of disclosure continues during proceedings

## 31.11

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.11] (1) Any duty of disclosure continues until the proceedings are concluded. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.11] (2) If documents to which that duty extends come to a party’s notice at any time during the proceedings, he must immediately notify every other party. ## Specific disclosure or inspection

## 31.12

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.12] (1) The court may make an order for specific disclosure or specific inspection. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.12] (2) An order for specific disclosure is an order that a party must do one or more of the following things –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.12] (a) disclose documents or classes of documents specified in the order;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.12] (b) carry out a search to the extent stated in the order;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.12] (c) disclose any documents located as a result of that search. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.12] (3) An order for specific inspection is an order that a party permit inspection of a document referred to in rule 31.3(2). [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.12] (Rule 31.3(2) allows a party to state in his disclosure statement that he will not permit inspection of a document on the grounds that it would be disproportionate to do so)

## Disclosure in stages

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > Disclosure in stages] 31.13 The parties may agree in writing, or the court may direct, that disclosure or inspection or both shall take place in stages. ## Documents referred to in statements of case etc. ## 31.14

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.14] (1) A party may inspect a document mentioned in –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.14] (a) a statement of case;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.14] (b) a witness statement;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.14] (c) a witness summary; or

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.14] (d) an affidavit (GL) . [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.14] (e) Revoked. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.14] (2) Subject to rule 35.10(4), a party may apply for an order for inspection of any document mentioned in an expert’s report which has not already been disclosed in the proceedings. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.14] (Rule 35.10(4) makes provision in relation to instructions referred to in an expert’s report)

## Inspection and copying of documents

## 31.15 Where a party has a right to inspect a document–

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.15 Where a party has a right to inspect a document–] (a) that party must give the party who disclosed the document written notice of his wish to inspect it;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.15 Where a party has a right to inspect a document–] (b) the party who disclosed the document must permit inspection not more than 7 days after the date on which he received the notice; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.15 Where a party has a right to inspect a document–] (c) that party may request a copy of the document and, if he also undertakes to pay reasonable copying costs, the party who disclosed the document must supply him with a copy not more than 7 days after the date on which he received the request. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.15 Where a party has a right to inspect a document–] (Rule 31.3 and 31.14 deal with the right of a party to inspect a document)

## Disclosure before proceedings start

## 31.16

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (1) This rule applies where an application is made to the court under any Act for disclosure before proceedings have started 1 . [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (2) The application must be supported by evidence. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (3) The court may make an order under this rule only where–

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (a) the respondent is likely to be a party to subsequent proceedings;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (b) the applicant is also likely to be a party to those proceedings;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (c) if proceedings had started, the respondent’s duty by way of standard disclosure, set out in rule 31.6, would extend to the documents or classes of documents of which the applicant seeks disclosure; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (d) disclosure before proceedings have started is desirable in order to –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (i) dispose fairly of the anticipated proceedings;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (ii) assist the dispute to be resolved without proceedings; or

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (iii) save costs. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (4) An order under this rule must –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (a) specify the documents or the classes of documents which the respondent must disclose; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (b) require him, when making disclosure, to specify any of those documents –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (i) which are no longer in his control; or

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (ii) in respect of which he claims a right or duty to withhold inspection. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (5) Such an order may –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (a) require the respondent to indicate what has happened to any documents which are no longer in his control; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.16] (b) specify the time and place for disclosure and inspection. ## Orders for disclosure against a person not a party

## 31.17

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (1) This rule applies where an application is made to the court under any Act for disclosure by a person who is not a party to the proceedings 2 . [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (2) The application must be supported by evidence. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (3) The court may make an order under this rule only where–

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (a) the documents of which disclosure is sought are likely to support the case of the applicant or adversely affect the case of one of the other parties to the proceedings; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (b) disclosure is necessary in order to dispose fairly of the claim or to save costs. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (4) An order under this rule must –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (a) specify the documents or the classes of documents which the respondent must disclose; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (b) require the respondent, when making disclosure, to specify any of those documents –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (i) which are no longer in his control; or

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (ii) in respect of which he claims a right or duty to withhold inspection. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (5) Such an order may –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (a) require the respondent to indicate what has happened to any documents which are no longer in his control; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.17] (b) specify the time and place for disclosure and inspection. ## Rules not to limit other powers of the court to order disclosure

## 31.18 Rules 31.16 and 31.17 do not limit any other power which the court may have to order –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.18 Rules 31.16 and 31.17 do not limit any other power which the court may have to order –] (a) disclosure before proceedings have started; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.18 Rules 31.16 and 31.17 do not limit any other power which the court may have to order –] (b) disclosure against a person who is not a party to proceedings. ## Claim to withhold inspection or disclosure of a document

## 31.19

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (1) A person may apply, without notice, for an order permitting him to withhold disclosure of a document on the ground that disclosure would damage the public interest. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (2) Unless the court orders otherwise, an order of the court under paragraph (1) –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (a) must not be served on any other person; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (b) must not be open to inspection by any person. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (3) A person who wishes to claim that he has a right or a duty to withhold inspection of a document, or part of a document, must state in writing –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (a) that he has such a right or duty; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (b) the grounds on which he claims that right or duty. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (4) The statement referred to in paragraph (3) must be made–

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (a) in the list in which the document is disclosed; or

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (b) if there is no list, to the person wishing to inspect the document. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (5) A party may apply to the court to decide whether a claim made under paragraph (3) should be upheld. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (6) For the purpose of deciding an application under paragraph (1) (application to withhold disclosure) or paragraph (3) (claim to withhold inspection) the court may –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (a) require the person seeking to withhold disclosure or inspection of a document to produce that document to the court; and

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (b) invite any person, whether or not a party, to make representations. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (7) An application under paragraph (1) or paragraph (5) must be supported by evidence. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.19] (8) This Part does not affect any rule of law which permits or requires a document to be withheld from disclosure or inspection on the ground that its disclosure or inspection would damage the public interest. ## Restriction on use of a privileged document inspection of which has been inadvertently allowed

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > Restriction on use of a privileged document inspection of which has been inadvertently allowed] 31.20 Where a party inadvertently allows a privileged (GL) document to be inspected, the party who has inspected the document may use it or its contents only with the permission of the court. ## Consequence of failure to disclose documents or permit inspection

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > Consequence of failure to disclose documents or permit inspection] 31.21 A party may not rely on any document which he fails to disclose or in respect of which he fails to permit inspection unless the court gives permission. ## Subsequent use of disclosed documents and completed Electronic Documents Questionnaires

## 31.22

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.22] (1) A party to whom a document has been disclosed may use the document only for the purpose of the proceedings in which it is disclosed, except where –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.22] (a) the document has been read to or by the court, or referred to, at a hearing which has been held in public;

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.22] (b) the court gives permission; or

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.22] (c) the party who disclosed the document and the person to whom the document belongs agree. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.22] (2) The court may make an order restricting or prohibiting the use of a document which has been disclosed, even where the document has been read to or by the court, or referred to, at a hearing which has been held in public. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.22] (3) An application for such an order may be made –

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.22] (a) by a party; or

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.22] (b) by any person to whom the document belongs. [PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.22] (4) For the purpose of this rule, an Electronic Documents Questionnaire which has been completed and served by another party pursuant to Practice Direction 31B is to be treated as if it is a document which has been disclosed. ## False disclosure statements

## 31.23

[PART 31 – DISCLOSURE AND INSPECTION OF DOCUMENTS > 31.23] (1) Proceedings for contempt of court may be brought against a person if he makes, or causes to be made, a false disclosure statement, without an honest belief in its truth.
